labels.zh-CN: 是否超过 2% 体重下降

details.formulaDescription: netLossLiters = preWeightKg − postWeightKg + fluidIntakeLiters. sweatRateLitersPerHour = netLossLiters / (durationMinutes / 60). bodyMassLossPercent = (preWeightKg − postWeightKg) / preWeightKg × 100. aboveTwoPercent = bodyMassLossPercent (rounded to 2 decimals) > 2. The weighing method for estimating individual sweat rate and the 2% body-mass-loss threshold come from the 2007 ACSM position stand on exercise and fluid replacement.
assumptions: The calculation assumes body mass change over the session reflects mainly sweat loss plus consumed fluid; urine, stool, substrate oxidation and metabolic water are not measured separately.
The method requires the same scale, similar clothing and a consistent weighing routine before and after exercise; scale precision limits the result.
Fluid intake must be the volume actually swallowed during the session, in litres.
A single session gives one estimate; sweat rate varies with weather, intensity, clothing, acclimatisation, menstrual cycle and illness.
The 2% flag follows the ACSM definition of excessive dehydration; it is a screening flag, not a diagnosis and not a drinking prescription.
The tool does not account for sodium losses, medical conditions, medication or pregnancy, and gives no medical advice.
details.rounding: Net loss and sweat rate are rounded to 2 decimal places; body mass loss percentage is rounded to 2 decimal places before the 2% flag is evaluated.
